pr_comments:
Even with the changes in this PR I think something is still missing.

I've made a build of the app that was initially affected by #36086 using this service-worker PR. 

On a 2019 generation LG OLED TV the service worker still completely breaks the app on the second load. First load is fine, but on reload nothing loads any more. It shows a "This page is not available" generic browser error. The LG TV runs Chromium 53. Clearing the browser cache resolves the problem for the first load, but on reload it breaks again.

I haven't been able to debug the TV to see what the actual error is, but it seems similar to `ERR_FAILED` that I've seen before even on desktop chrome.

**Edit**: Found what the error on the TV is, it's this: https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/20756

I wish we could implement option (b) (from https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/20756#issuecomment-386315924), but it didn't get traction :grin:

I am a little concerned about monkey-patching such basic APIs (i.e. `waitUntil()` and `respondWith()`) for everyone (versus just for those needing it). Is there a way to feature-detect this?

In any case, feel free to create a separate PR for that fix and we can discuss there.
(I'd rather keep this on a separate PR, since it is an unrelated issue and potentially controversial too :grin:)
Hey, @andreialecu, would you have time/interest to move this forward? (Or should someone else take over?)

I could, but maybe it's easier for you to take it over yourself if you have time yourself?

Allow edits is on. The polyfill turns out is more important for our use case. As mentioned previously, all LG TV's before 2020 need it. They cannot be updated so nothing can be done about getting angular+service-worker not completely blow up on them. I'd be interested in a solution for that as well, because kiosk/informational apps are broken otherwise (other TVs/boxes have the same issue)

Chromium version for webOS releases, for reference:
http://webostv.developer.lge.com/discover/specifications/web-engine/

For Samsung TVs, 2018 and older won't work either: 
https://developer.samsung.com/smarttv/develop/specifications/web-engine-specifications.html

issue_context.title: Service Worker "Quota exceeded" can break all JS (ERR_FAILED)
issue_context.body:
# 🐞 bug report ### Affected Package The issue is caused by package @angular/service-worker ### Is this a regression? Not sure ### Description The service worker fails to load core JS files with `DOMException: Quota exceeded.` This results in just a white page being shown, with a broken app. Angular 9.0.4 Chromium 80 ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/697707/76769191-ca076080-67a4-11ea-8690-93f4030e0a5b.png) ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/697707/76769205-cf64ab00-67a4-11ea-8f2a-ccaaa3a407e2.png) I've migrated from a custom workbox based serviceworker to the angular native service worker and now running into this. Force reloading (`ctrl+f5`) makes everything load, but the error returns on the next normal load. After using DevTools to debug it, I found that the error is `DOMException: Quota exceeded.` and occurs in this block: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/697707/76770457-acd39180-67a6-11ea-8f76-3c1cf34f2c14.png) ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction Hard to reproduce unfortunately, needs low disk space or a big app being cached. ## 🔥 Exception or Error 

The FetchEvent for ".../runtime-es2015.91c3f469886b8efa1fca.js" resulted in a network error response: the promise was rejected.
Promise.then (async)
onFetch @ ngsw-worker.js:1993
(anonymous) @ ngsw-worker.js:1928
## 🌍 Your Environment **Angular Version:** 
9.0.4
**Anything else relevant?** Might be related to #21412 and #33793 which both appear fixed. I'm not sure what the right fix here would be, I think fallback to network might be appropriate rather than completely failing the request.
comments:
Possibly relevant, from Chrome DevTools:

```js
await navigator.storage.estimate()
{"quota":22767180,"usage":22767180,"usageDetails":{"caches":22625280,"serviceWorkerRegistrations":141900}}
```

Also relevant, cleaning up more disk space cleared up this error. Previously only around 600 MB were free on the system partition. 

Freeing up more space (up to 1.45GB) resulted in the error going away, as the quota was increased by Chrome:

```
await navigator.storage.estimate()
"{"quota":477935948,"usage":24512844,"usageDetails":{"caches":24370944,"serviceWorkerRegistrations":141900}}"
```

Also helpful was https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/31256#issuecomment-506507021 in order to prevent duplicate JS files from being cached.

Also possibly related: https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/26042

I'm seeing an additional issue with caching, it seems like the old version of the app remains cached after an update:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/697707/76777750-5c156600-67b1-11ea-98af-81293e8d633c.png)

```
await navigator.storage.estimate()
"{"quota":507196236,"usage":46687052,"usageDetails":{"caches":46545152,"serviceWorkerRegistrations":141900}}"
```
Usage has doubled.

Is this normal? Should previous versions be purged from the cache?

Perhaps we should wrap `table.write()` calls inside `sync()` in try-catch and degrade to safe mode if something is catched.
It also makes sense to catch and log this errors inside `table.write()` to prevent this kind of errors from happening once and for all 🤔

As for old cache versions, I believe they should be cleaned in the background, after successful sw installation and update cheking, see https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/168a393589f80bd2fa6fb3fb6235754c5e75a384/packages/service-worker/worker/src/driver.ts#L135 and https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/168a393589f80bd2fa6fb3fb6235754c5e75a384/packages/service-worker/worker/src/driver.ts#L876

Seems like the old cache entries were purged eventually. Not sure why the initial update didn't trigger the cleanup properly, but I assume a subsequent initialization of the service worker properly cleaned things up.

The Quota Exceeded error however is troubling. Especially for things like tablets/phones or Smart TVs with limited storage. 

For example our app has a kiosk-like module and one customer which uses Android devices reported `ERR_FAILED` errors on their entire Android device fleet while just loading the main "index.html" page. I assume it is related to this as I wasn't able to debug it further without going on premise.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/697707/76841553-9cbcc000-6841-11ea-9a92-1cf392a45f5f.png)

@andreialecu If you have ngsw in business-critical applications, i can suggest removing it or sticking to workbox. It's not the first ngsw error that cripples the whole application. Most common ones are fixed, but you can never be sure until ALL `CacheStorage` write calls are wrapped.

As you've found out the caches are indeed cleaned up. Regarding the `Quota exceeded` error, as @apocalyp0sys said, there seems to be a couple more places where we need to handle it correctly when calling [Driver#sync()][1] (or rather cover all call sites of [CacheTable#write()][2]).

I don't think I will be able to get to it any time soon (due to other priorities), but if someone wants to take it on, I would be happy to help/review :grin:

[1]: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/9e70bcb34f91d439f5203dc22a44f323d02c4648/packages/service-worker/worker/src/driver.ts#L850
[2]: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/9e70bcb34f91d439f5203dc22a44f323d02c4648/packages/service-worker/worker/src/db-cache.ts#L67

@gkalpak I opened a PR, mind checking it out?

This is severely broken for us especially on Smart-TV browsers with older versions of Chrome.
Thx, @andreialecu 😍 I'll take a look asap (probably tomorrow).

@gkalpak kind reminder, hopefully you have some time :)

I assume minor changes might need to be made, so let me know what you think and I'll get to them asap.

review_comments: We shouldn't end up here if `DriverReadyState` is not `NORMAL` in the first place. Can you explain what code-path could lead us here?
No, this is not necessary. By returning here, the SW signals that it is not interested in handling the request, so the browser can go to the network, which is what we want when in `SAFE_MODE`.

I don't think this is the right way to handle this. We should have thrown an appropriate error and then decide here whether we need to enter `EXISTING_CLIENTS_ONLY` or `SAFE_MODE`. We should try to minimize the places where the `DriverReadyState` can change.

This shouldn't be necessary. The error should be caught in [ensureInitialized()][1] and [when necessary][2] the SW would respond with a network fetch.

[1]: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/91b7a3192559ba312ec7df6f96693751fec721cf/packages/service-worker/worker/src/driver.ts#L299-L306
[2]: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/91b7a3192559ba312ec7df6f96693751fec721cf/packages/service-worker/worker/src/driver.ts#L409
